name: Qatar
summary: Territorial system with no tax on employment income and no tax on capital gains, dividends, interest or rent for individuals who do not carry on a taxable business activity in Qatar. Gains on Qatari real estate and securities are exempt for residents unless part of a taxable activity (non-residents pay 10% on Qatar-source gains). No inheritance, gift or wealth tax; no VAT yet (a draft VAT law has been approved by the Cabinet but not published). Corporate tax 10% on foreign-owned profits; 15% DMTT/IIR for large MNEs from 2025. About 83 treaties, none with the US. Property purchase of QAR 3.65m+ in designated areas gives permanent-residency benefits.

regimes.name: Qatar tax residence
regimes.description: No tax on individuals' investment income or gains; territorial system.
regimes.eligibility: Any legal resident; no special status required.

capital_gains.summary: No capital gains tax for resident individuals on real estate or securities not held as part of a taxable activity in Qatar.
capital_gains.important_exceptions: Non-residents are taxed at 10% on Qatar-source capital gains. A capital gains return is due within 30 days of a sale where tax applies. A business 'activity' is broadly defined (including exploitation of movable or immovable property), so an individual running a Qatar business could be taxed at 10% on its income.

sources.title: Qatar - Individual - Taxes on personal income (last reviewed 17 Sep 2026)

capital_gains.rate_basis: Qatar income tax is territorial; PwC: gains on disposal of real estate and securities are exempt unless part of a taxable activity. Foreign gains are outside the territorial scope.
capital_gains.professional_trader: An individual whose dealing amounts to a taxable 'activity' in Qatar would be taxed at 10% on that Qatar-source business income; passive portfolio investment is not taxed.
capital_gains.foreign_assets: Foreign-source gains are outside the territorial scope.

dividends.summary: No tax on dividends for individuals: dividends from profits already taxed in Qatar or from exempt companies are not taxable, and foreign dividends are outside the territorial scope.
dividends.rate_basis: Territorial system; PwC income determination: dividends not taxable if paid from taxed or exempt profits; bank interest not taxable for individuals without a taxable activity.
dividends.withholding_outbound: No WHT on dividends paid by Qatari companies.
dividends.treaty_network: About 83 treaties listed by PwC; no treaty with the United States, so US dividends held directly bear 30% US WHT.

sources.title: Qatar - Individual - Other taxes (last reviewed 17 Sep 2026)

wealth_tax.property_tax_note: No property tax. Owners pay registration fees on property transfers and landlords pay lease registration fees (rates not verified).

inheritance.summary: No inheritance, estate or gift tax.
inheritance.important_exceptions: Succession, not tax, is the issue: personal status (family) law based on Sharia governs inheritance of Muslims, with fixed shares (a son typically takes twice a daughter's share) and at most one third freely disposable by will to non-heirs. How estates of non-Muslim foreigners are handled (home-country law, own religious rules, or Sharia by default) was not verified for this country; non-Muslim families should take local legal advice and hold portfolio assets outside the country or through a structure with a clear governing law.

sources.title: Qatar - Individual - Other taxes (last reviewed 17 Sep 2026)

open_questions: Treatment of non-Muslim foreigners' estates under Qatari family law (Law 22/2006) not verified.
inheritance.foreign_assets: No tax on any asset, local or foreign.

residency.tax_residency_test: Qatar Tax Law (amended by Law 11/2022): resident if the individual has a permanent home in Qatar, or lives in Qatar more than 183 days (continuous or not) in a year, or is a Qatari national. Residence matters little for individuals because tax is territorial and investment income is untaxed.

routes.name: Property-owner permanent residency benefits (first class)
routes.requirements: Purchase of property worth at least QAR 3,650,000 (about USD 1m) in designated areas gives permanent-residency benefits including health, education and investment rights (Aqarat).

routes.name: Property-owner residency (second class)
routes.requirements: Purchase of property worth at least QAR 730,000 (about USD 200,000) gives residency tied to the property (Aqarat).

routes.name: Employment / company residence
routes.requirements: Residence permit through an employer or a company (e.g. Qatar Financial Centre entity).

sources.title: Own real estate - Investor's journey (residency for property owners)

corporate.summary: Flat 10% CIT on Qatar-source profits of foreign-owned entities; entities wholly owned by Qatari and resident GCC nationals currently pay no CIT; oil operations at least 35%. DMTT and IIR (Pillar Two) apply for fiscal years from 1 January 2025; no UTPR. No WHT on dividends.
corporate.special_zones: Qatar Financial Centre (QFC) and Qatar Free Zones have separate regimes (not verified in this pass).

sources.title: Qatar - Corporate - Taxes on corporate income

us_citizen_notes: US citizens remain fully US-taxed; no Qatar-US income tax treaty.
open_questions: Property registration fee rates not verified.
VAT introduction date unknown (draft law approved, not published).
